title: Trace a dynamic request through normal and degraded paths
description: Select a scenario to see which work is required before the response, which failures are contained, and what the user experiences.

nodes.label: Browser or API client
nodes.detail: Starts one request with a client-visible deadline and renders the returned result or explicit error.

nodes.label: CDN edge
nodes.detail: Terminates transport, applies coarse protection, serves safe cache hits, and routes misses to origin.

nodes.label: API gateway
nodes.detail: Enforces route policy, propagates the remaining deadline, and chooses the owning application service.

nodes.label: Identity provider
nodes.detail: Supplies remote identity or authorization evidence when local token verification is not sufficient.

nodes.label: Order service
nodes.detail: Builds the response, owns bounded dependency calls, and returns a safe fallback or clear failure before its deadline expires.

nodes.label: Read cache
nodes.detail: Serves reusable order-summary data quickly. A miss has bounded fallback to the authoritative database.

nodes.label: Orders database
nodes.detail: Owns durable order state and must be protected from stampedes, long waits, and unbounded retries.

nodes.label: Event stream
nodes.detail: Accepts analytics and audit events outside the response path, with an explicit buffer-or-drop policy under pressure.

nodes.label: Analytics worker
nodes.detail: Consumes event data for reporting and must not delay the customer response when it is unavailable.

scenarios.label: Edge cache hit
scenarios.summary: A cacheable response ends at the edge. Origin, identity, and data capacity are not used for this request.
scenarios.result: The user receives the cached response quickly. Cache freshness rules, invalidation, and authorization boundaries determine whether this shortcut is safe.

scenarios.label: Dynamic cache hit
scenarios.summary: A protected request reaches origin, verifies authorization, and reads a hot summary from the cache. Telemetry leaves asynchronously.
scenarios.result: The response is dynamic but avoids database I/O. A slow analytics worker does not add to the critical path.

scenarios.label: Database tail spike
scenarios.summary: The cache misses and the database becomes slow. The application and database are degraded while the deadline limits how long the caller waits.
scenarios.result: Return a contractually safe cached or partial result when possible, otherwise fail before the caller deadline. Do not let retries multiply database load.

scenarios.label: Identity outage
scenarios.summary: Remote authorization evidence is unavailable, so the gateway never sends this protected request to the order service or database.
scenarios.result: The request fails fast with a clear protected-route error. Keeping the downstream path inactive preserves order-service and database capacity.

scenarios.label: Analytics outage
scenarios.summary: The customer response remains on the dynamic cache-hit path while the non-critical analytics worker is unavailable.
scenarios.result: The product response remains available. The event stream follows its explicit buffer, retry, or drop policy instead of turning a reporting outage into customer latency.
